hypothesis: The exponential-family concern parameterisation on the 4-bit Boolean world of Instrument 4 obeys Theorem CG-1 (Fisher matrix = beta^2 * diag(sech^2(beta c_i)) on every fiber) and Theorem CG-2 (holonomy of the non-exact concern-1-form alpha + epsilon(-c_2 dc_1) around a loop equals epsilon times the signed enclosed area) exactly on the pre-registered grid.

controls.description: The empirical Fisher matrix computed by direct enumeration over the 4-element fiber is checked against the closed-form beta^2 * diag(sech^2(beta c_i)) at every (c, z) in the 4x4 grid; agreement to 1e-12 required.
Because T_1 = 2 x_0 - 1 and T_2 = 2 x_2 - 1 read disjoint bit pairs, their covariance is zero on every fiber; verified directly for each grid point.
The added 1-form -epsilon * c_2 dc_1 has curl +epsilon, so Green's theorem predicts holonomy = epsilon * (signed area enclosed). Rectangle and triangle both verified.
Line integrals are computed by trapezoidal quadrature with 500 steps per edge; error bound falls well within the 1e-3 gate tolerance.

gates.criterion: Maximum absolute difference between empirical Fisher and beta^2 * diag(sech^2(beta c_i)) over the 4x4 grid is below 1e-12.
Off-diagonal entries of the empirical Fisher matrix are exactly zero at every grid point.
Holonomy around the unit rectangle in c-space at z=(1,1) is within 1e-3 of epsilon = 0.3.
Holonomy around the unit triangle at z=(1,1) is within 1e-3 of epsilon/2 = 0.15.
